findings.title: $5M RANSOM FOR LEGACY LOGISTICS BOX
findings.comment: WhiteArmor claims 100GB of driver passwords and IMEIs off an acquired subsidiary, Maersk says relax nothing sensitive leaked, ye olde "isolated legacy system" excuse never gets old.

findings.title: BYOD GANG CLAIMS A MILLION SSNs
findings.comment: New-ish crew BYOD brags "we have your entire estate," university shuts down wifi campus-wide and still won't say if they paid, silence be the house style now.

findings.title: THE GENTLEMEN POST FRENCH SCHOOL GROUP
findings.comment: Work-study education group added to the leak-site ledger a day after the breach, details thin as ever but the extortion clock's already ticking.

findings.title: CALIFORNIA HOSPITAL HIT BY SCARLETTGROUP
findings.comment: Ridgecrest's regional hospital lands on a leak site from a crew nobody tracked a month ago, proof these gangs multiply faster than the patches meant to stop 'em.

findings.title: APACHE 2.4.71 FIXES CRITICAL MOD_HTTP2 RCE
findings.comment: A race in assign_headers turns any HTTP/2 server 2.4.55-2.4.70 into a rowboat, found by Anthropic's scanner an' Google. 2.4.71 dropped Nov 11 - hoist it aboard before someone else does.

findings.title: CYBERSTRIKEAI AWS INTRUSION SPAWNS TWO NEW DETECTION RULES
findings.comment: 56 API calls in 141 milliseconds across four accounts - no human types that fast, matey. Bulk user-data an' GetCallerIdentity ES

findings.title: SANSAR ROOTKIT FAKES 0% GPU WHILE MINING YOUR FLEET
findings.comment: Rust orchestrator, ftrace rootkit, swapped NVML library lyin' about utilization while the hold fills with coin. YARA an' hashes in the post - an' lock up yer exposed Ray agents.

findings.title: DOJ/EUROPOL SMASH GOOTLOADER BOTNET
findings.comment: Ye old malware loader since 2018 finally got the plank — 100+ servers scrubbed, 235 seized overall, all fer the low price of $28.8M in Yankee ransomware losses it caused.

findings.title: FSB CREW HID 'CEREAL' IN EXCHANGE SERVERS
findings.comment: Turla parked a mail-sniffing backdoor inside Kazakh and Romanian Exchange servers, fishing fer NATO and EU correspondence — and the compromised box itself was the C2, clever bilge rats.

findings.title: ROMANIA CONFIRMS IT CAUGHT RUSSIAN SPIES IN ITS INBOX
findings.comment: Romania's SRI admitted Turla camped in a government mail system since December 2025, but swears no NATO secrets were plundered — arr, "no exfiltration identified" be the oldest line in the harbor.

findings.title: NK HACKERS RESUME DREAM-JOB DRONE HUNT
findings.comment: Lazarus be back since June with fake BAE Systems job offers fer European drone-makers — phishing fer parts while Pyongyang builds its own sky fleet, mateys.

findings.title: KAZAKH-LINKED CREW RAN AI SPY AGENT
findings.comment: Silent Lynx let a DeepSeek-powered agent dubbed Hermes do the recon and cleanup on Tajikistan's railway — even the spies be outsourcing to the machines now, arr.

findings.title: CHINA-NEXUS SPEAR-PHISH SPOTTED IN CZECHIA
findings.comment: Moderate-confidence China crew baited Czech and Taiwanese officials with fake paperwork, stashing its AZUREVEIL ransom in Azure Blob Storage — hiding the loot in the cloud itself, sneaky devils.

findings.title: RANSOMWARE CRIPPLES BELARUSIAN CLOUD HOST
findings.comment: ActiveCloud's customers — news sites, pizza outfits — spent days dark after encryption hit, yet no crew has claimed the prize and no data theft was found, a ghost attack in a rough neighborhood.

findings.title: RANSOMWARE CREW LISTS FIVE BANKS, TWO CONFIRM
findings.comment: The Storm crew bragged of breaching five banks worth $6.1B, but only Sawyer Savings and one credit union fessed up — 16,069 souls' Social Security numbers set adrift.

findings.title: TELECOM GUTTED VIA UNAUTH XML BUG
findings.comment: A Chinese-speaking crew ran a jailbroken DeepSeek model through an unauthenticated XXE to loot a European telco's private keys, then dropped Sliver, Chisel and a Behinder web shell for good measure — efficient scallywags.

findings.title: EIGHTH CHROME ZERO-DAY OF THE YEAR SUNK
findings.comment: Google patched a use-after-free in the XML engine that attackers were already riding in the wild, marking Chrome's eighth zero-day this year — at this rate the browser needs its own KEV subscription.

findings.title: FILE TRANSFER BOX HANDS OUT FREE ADMIN
findings.comment: CVE-2026-123218 lets any authenticated nobody craft a message into full admin rights on IBM's Aspera Faspex — a 9.8 CVSS party favor already being exploited before most admins read the bulletin.

findings.title: SSLVPN MFA BYPASSED WITH ONE FACTOR
findings.comment: SonicWall's SAML-enforced MFA turns out to be more of a strong suggestion — CVE-2026-19868 lets anyone with one valid credential sail straight past it, now added to KEV with exploitation reports already in.

findings.title: OPENAI ARMS BOTH SIDES WITH AI PENTESTER
findings.comment: OpenAI unveiled Daybreak Red Team, a fleet of agents that hunts and proves web app vulnerabilities on its "Critical risk" GPT-6 Cyber model — handy for defenders, and a free preview of tomorrow's attacker tooling.

findings.title: VOIP PLATFORM CODE INJECTION UNDER FIRE
findings.comment: SignalWire FreeSWITCH's CVE-2026-116779 code injection flaw landed on KEV alongside Aspera and OpenSSH, proof that telephony infrastructure is still everyone's favorite soft target.
